name: Adrenaline 30

date.source: The fed's own news desk dates it Sunday 11 July 2004: its post of Saturday 10 July 2004 announces the show's World Title match for "this Sunday" at Adrenaline 30, and its post of 26 June 2004 gave the roster a fourteen-day break after the show of 20 June, which puts Adrenaline 29 on 4 July. The write-up carries no date line; it counts itself "Three weeks away from the pay-per-view" (Eve of Destruction, 1 August 2004). Argyle's booking record dates it 4 July 2004, the Sunday of Adrenaline 29 (#sources-disagree).

notes: The World Title match between the champion, Karina Wolfenden, and Tessa Windsor is ended by Magnum Wolf's chair attack as the bell sounds; the write-up never rules a result, so the row carries none. Of the Silver and Skywolf match the write-up says only that it "basically ended in a draw".

name: Adrenaline 31

date.source: The fed's own news desk dates it Sunday 18 July 2004: its post of 16 July 2004 looks ahead to Adrenaline 31 and back on Adrenaline 30, and its post of 21 July 2004 reports the show's Hessian challenge "As seen on RPW Adrenaline 31". The write-up carries no date line; it has Magnum Wolf "in 2 weeks" from his World Title match at the supercard of 1 August 2004. Argyle's booking record dates it 11 July 2004 (#sources-disagree).

notes: One short passage of the write-up (part of a sentence, in Carys v Hessian) is withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest stands.

name: Adrenaline 32

date.source: The fed's own news desk dates it Sunday 25 July 2004: its post of Tuesday 20 July 2004 says none of the Old School Elite was yet booked for Adrenaline 32, and its news list carries "Fourth Opposition Member Revealed Hours Before AD 32!" under 25 July 2004. The write-up carries no date line; it is "seven days away" from the Eve of Destruction supercard of 1 August 2004, and its ten-man tag match was proposed "the Tuesday before". Argyle's booking record dates it 18 July 2004 (#sources-disagree).

matches.stipulation: Ten-Man Tag Team Match (no time limit, no count-outs)

notes: Brian Arson is first counted the winner of the World Title match after Magnum Wolf knocks Karina Wolfenden's foot off the rope; the referee, shown the replay, restarts the match and Karina pins Arson with a small package. The row records the deciding fall. The ten-man tag is billed five men a side; Cisco Milloy enters unbilled to fill the vacancy.

name: Adrenaline 1

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 1, a Sunday), and the write-up itself corroborates it: it is "the inaugural presentation of Rush Pro-Wrestling's Sunday Adrenaline" and "the FIRST ever broadcast of Rush Pro-Wrestling", and its Karina Wolfenden video ends on the slate "RPW / 09/11/03". The write-up is the fed's own TV-card page on rpw.sheepsden.com, from our Wayback capture of 10 December 2003.

notes: Jason Marah v Carys ends when the referee calls for the bell after Carys's shovel attack; the text names no winner and no disqualification, so the row carries no outcome. Totakoxe Salvador v Mike Marvelous ends on the referee's third arm-drop count in a camel clutch; the text says only that Salvador "has defeated" Marvelous and names no submission, so the row carries a winner and no method. One sentence of the write-up (in the backstage scene where Carys meets Sam Alotti) is withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest of the scene stands.

name: Adrenaline 2

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 2, the Sunday after the first show), and the write-up corroborates it: "our second broadcast of Sunday Adrenaline", "only the second show in the history of Rush Pro-Wrestling", and it opens by replaying the finish of the first show's ladder match as "last week". The write-up is the fed's own TV-card page on rpw.sheepsden.com, from our Wayback capture of 10 December 2003.

notes: The show opens with a replay of the finish of the first show's Eclipse Title ladder match, which is counted on that show. Alyssa Sanders v Ashley Winters is broken up by a shovel attack before it begins, and the text rules no result.

name: Adrenaline 4

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 4). The capture's own file name on the fed's archive is cat_ad113003 (11/30/03), and the text corroborates the count: Peter Maxwell says "After just 4 weeks, RPW is over", and the Eclipse Title match opens on "the Title he won last week". The fed's own news of 23 November 2003 calls the show before it "Sunday's 3rd edition of Adrenaline", and its news of 30 November 2003 says that night's broadcast was tape-delayed to the Monday, the show itself being held on the Sunday. The write-up is the fed's own Adrenaline archive page on rpw.sheepsden.com, from our Wayback capture of 10 December 2003.

notes: Peter Maxwell and a mystery partner against Steven Caldera and Kimbusa is announced and then becomes a four-man ambush with no bell, so it is filed as a segment and not a match.

name: Adrenaline 7

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 7). The page's own file name in the fed's Adrenaline archive on angrypete.net is cat_ad122103 (12/21/03), and the text looks ahead to the Genesis show of "January Fourth". The fed's own news post of 22 December 2003 reports what happened "As Adrenaline 7 went off the air" and the Eclipse Title won back "last night". The write-up is that show's page in the Adrenaline archive on angrypete.net, from our Wayback capture of 29 November 2004.

notes: Jackson Rust v Alyssa Sanders and Sam Alotti ends when the referee rings the bell on Tessa Windsor's interference; the text names no winner and no disqualification, so the row carries no outcome. The fifteen-man battle royal announced for the main event is not held: Peter Maxwell cancels it on the air and proclaims himself the first RPW World Champion.

name: Adrenaline 24

date.source: The fed's own news desk dates it Sunday 16 May 2004: its post of 23 May 2004 says Adrienne Diamond "was attacked last week on Adrenaline 24", its post of 18 May says that Sunday's Adrenaline was taped but kept off the air, and its post of 22 May reports Cisco Milloy's Six Finger Crisco ULTRA demonstration on that Adrenaline. The write-up carries no date line; it puts the Kannon Effect pay-per-view (23 May) "next week", and the Adrenaline 25 write-up of 30 May calls its events "two weeks ago". Argyle's booking record dates it 2 May 2004, a Sunday on which the fed's news says no show was held (#sources-disagree).

notes: Magnum Wolf and Christian Crawford, the last match (billed under the unit title "Twenty Fucking Five"), is Wolf's open challenge answered by Crawford: Wolf destroys him without a pin ("This piece of shit isn't even worth pinning"), Lee Wilkinson and Willie Smythe (Rule Britannia) come out and are beaten, and Christian Kannon and Karina Wolfenden are hurt; no bell rules a result and the build records no decision, so the row names the two competitors Argyle's own rows give and carries no outcome. Shawn Stewart and Exceptional Dave Hurst v Steven Silver and Cisco Milloy ends when Silver hits Stewart with a chair and the text says he and Cisco are "DQ'ed", so the winners are Stewart and Hurst. Powell v Tessa Windsor is not a title match: Windsor is the number one contender to the Mid-South Title and Powell wins by a small package after using a roll of quarters his secretary, Nichelle Yvette Clarkson, has passed him. Two short passages of the write-up (a sentence and a word, in the segment "Step Into My Errr…Office") are withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest stands.

name: Adrenaline 25

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it 30 May 2004 (Adrenaline 25, a Sunday), and the text carries it: it names its own number ("Adrenaline 25" in the Eclipse Title match, and "ADrenaline 24" for the previous show), it opens "A week after the Kannon Effect" (the pay-per-view of 23 May 2004, as the fed's news of 7 May 2004 moved it), and Gaz Green says the Nerezza character's "birthday was on Saturday May 29th". The fed's own news posts of 1 and 2 June 2004 report what followed it "as Adrenaline 25 went off the air". The write-up carries no date line of its own.

notes: Steven Silver v Tessa Windsor, billed as a Mid-South Title match with Windsor as champion, ends when referee Chris Faircount signals for the bell as Silver strangles her; the text names no winner and does not use the word disqualification, so the row carries no outcome (the build files a disqualification win for Windsor). Cisco Milloy v Shawn Stewart collapses into Dave Gibson's ambush and Pain's attack and the text rules no result; the row carries none. The billed Freak Show v The Forsaken is not held: its unit reads "Yeah. This didn't happen. The Forsaken are a myth." and is a segment, not a match. In the Eclipse Title five-way Gideon Poe pins the champion, Carys. One short passage of the write-up (part of a sentence, in the Eclipse Title five-way) is withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest stands.

name: Adrenaline 8

date.source: The fed's own write-up of the show. The page's own file name (cat_ad010404, read as 01-04-04) and the booking date agree, and the text bears it out: it opens on "After a 2 week absence because of the Christmas break, the fans are back in abundance", a character says "I tured 17 on New Years!", and the card announces Genesis for "A week tonight". The text never gives its own number; the fed's own news gives it: its post of 22 December 2003 looks ahead from Adrenaline 7 to "Adrenaline 8", its post of 23 December cancels that week's show, and its post of 3 January 2004 previews this card's Seth Masters v Kohana for "This week on Adrenaline".

notes: An interview on the card tells Gideon Poe he faces Totakoxe Salvador "tonight in a singles match"; the write-up carries no such match, so the row has none. Two sentences of the write-up (in the corridor scene where Carys confronts Tessa Windsor and Jackson Rust) are withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest of the scene stands.

name: Adrenaline 9

date.source: The fed's own write-up of the show. The page's own file name (cat_ad011804, read as 01-18-04) and the booking date agree, and the text bears it out: it is "the first showing of Adrenaline post Genesis", Genesis is "last week" (and the 4 January show announces it for "A week tonight", so Genesis fell on 11 January). The text never gives its own number.

notes: The write-up opens on a replay of the closing minutes of the previous week's Genesis main event; the replayed match makes no row on this show. The last segment ends with the source's own note that the remainder was removed for its graphic nature. A few quoted words of a joke in the narration (in The Forsaken's entrance) are withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest of the sentence stands.

date.source: The fed's own write-up of the show. Neither the page nor its file name (cat_ad10) carries a date, so the booking date rests on the order of the texts: the page calls itself "Adrenaline 10", has Genesis already past, and speaks of the 18 January show's events as "last week" (the Eclipse rules change, the handicap loss, the loss to Invincible Gabe, the attack that cost the fed its television slot).

name: Adrenaline 21

date.source: Argyle's booking record dates the show Sunday 18 April 2004 (his label for it is blank). The write-up's own words are consistent with that date: it says it is "over a week since Easter Sunday" (Easter fell on 11 April 2004), and its main event is "the second main event of the Christian Kannon era in RPW". The write-up never states its number; the fed's own page for it is its Adrenaline 21 page (cat_ad21), the fed's own news post of 21 April 2004 opens "After AD21", and the next write-up calls the show between them "the Adrenaline 22". The page carries no date line of its own.

notes: The six-man World Title match changes format twice: it opens as a tag-format match, Christian Kannon then rules no disqualification, no count-outs and no tagging, and the first finish is disputed (Magnum Wolf makes Gideon Poe tap out as Invincible Gabe is counted for the pin on Violence Jack), so Kannon restarts it as sudden death between Wolf and Gabe with himself as referee, and Gabe wins that fall. The row records the deciding fall.

name: Adrenaline 23

date.source: The fed's own news desk dates it Sunday 9 May 2004: its post of Friday 7 May 2004 says a water main break had closed the offices and "even forced the cancellation of Adrenaline last Sunday" (2 May), and that there would be two more shows before "The Kannon Effect", "now on May 23rd"; its post of 10 May 2004 reports what was said "after Adrenaline 23". The write-up carries no date line, and it was written for 2 May: a character reads "May 2nd" off a calendar, the owner's draw names the Kannon Effect "on May 16th", its date before the move, and the show of the week before is "the Adrenaline 22". Argyle's booking record dates it 25 April 2004, the Sunday of Adrenaline 22 (#sources-disagree).

notes: The Re:plica v Rule Britannia match is a tag-format match in which Willie Smythe is eliminated by submission and Lee Wilkinson is then pinned; the row records the deciding fall. The four-corners match is won by The Freak Show, Mick Pepper pinning Halfton.

name: Adrenaline 17

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 17, a Sunday). The write-up carries no date of its own (it is that show's page in the Adrenaline archive on angrypete.net, file cat_ad17), but its text anchors the week: it opens on "Last Sunday at Maximum Overdrive, I did what needed to be done", and the next show's write-up (28 March) calls the tag-title win at Maximum Overdrive "Two weeks ago" and Steven Silver's attack on this show "last week". The write-up is from our Wayback capture of 2 June 2004.

notes: Jason O'Neil v The Dread Pirate Roberts is billed as the main event and does not take place: Gideon Poe, refereeing, starts a ten-count on O'Neil outside the ring and Rush Mason's entrance interrupts it at nine, and the show ends on Mason's announcement; the text rules no result, so the row carries none. Chris Storm v Malphas ends on a five-count: Storm orders the referee to count to five and the ring announcer proclaims him "STILL RPW Mid South champion"; the text does not say the belt is on the line. One sentence of the write-up (in Carys's promo, "Vengeance Shall Be Hers") is withheld from the served page and marked in place; her words stand.

name: Adrenaline 18

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (a Sunday; his record gives it no number). The fed's own news post of 4 April 2004 calls it Adrenaline 18 ("last Week on Adrenaline 18"), as does the page's own file name in the fed's Adrenaline archive (cat_ad18, after cat_ad17 of 21 March), and the text anchors the date: Rush Mason thanks the fans "for lining my pockets for the past 20 weeks" and Little Al says "the last 20 weeks", and 20 weeks after the fed's first show of 9 November 2003 is 28 March 2004; it also says "Two weeks ago, Invincibleness~! did the impossible" (the Maximum Overdrive tag-title win) and refers to Steven Silver's attack "last week". The fed's news of 29 March 2004 reports what was said "At what he believed to be the last ever Adrenaline". The write-up is that show's page in the Adrenaline archive on angrypete.net, from our Wayback capture of 2 June 2004.

notes: Steven Silver v Matt Jackson ends when Silver lands a low blow in front of the referee, who calls for the bell as Jackson goes down; the text names no winner and does not use the word disqualification, so the row carries no outcome. Chris Storm v Shawn Stewart ends when the referee makes a ten-count over an unconscious Storm at Stewart's order.

name: Adrenaline 20

date.source: The fed's own booking record dates it (Adrenaline 20, a Sunday), and the text calls itself "the 20th edition of Adrenaline". It refers to a show one week earlier ("last week", "7 days ago": Christian Kannon's first words as the fed's backer and his Hallmark on Gideon Poe) whose events are not on the held show of 28 March, which fits Adrenaline 19 of 4 April between them, a show whose write-up this wing does not hold: the fed's own news of 5 April 2004 reports it ("This past Adrenaline") and books this card's Rampage v Violence Jack for "the April 11th edition of Adrenaline", and its news of 14 April 2004 speaks of "after AD20 had aired". The write-up is that show's page in the Adrenaline archive on angrypete.net (file cat_ad20), from our Wayback capture of 2 June 2004.

notes: Invincibleness~! v The Phantom Swerve~! is announced for the tag titles and ends when the referee counts out the three masked challengers as they walk out; they have no id, so the row lists only the champions as participants and gives them as the winners. Vangellus Oxios v Hessian is stopped by a disqualification call on Oxios and restarted as a no-disqualification match on Little Al's ruling; Hessian pins Oxios. Scott Matthews v Violence Jack ends in a double pin, announced as a draw. One sentence of the write-up (in Carys v Quinton Dufresne) is withheld from the served page and marked in place; the rest of the match stands.
